_meta.provenance: 25 dual-method (slow cooker / pressure cooker) recipes extracted from import/The_Master_Pot_Collection.pdf (2026-07-10). Descriptions and fun facts from the PDF; per-recipe reference URL from the PDF's Reference line. Methods carry per-method cookTime/totalTime because slow-cooker and pressure-cooker durations differ by an order of magnitude.

notes.methods: kind traditional = Slow Cooker, kind rapid = Pressure Cooker (Instant Pot). Published as sibling version records per the Phase 6 dessert precedent.
notes.enrichment: serves estimated from ingredient quantities; diet via ingredient scan (conservative: soy sauce / flour / noodles block gluten-free); cuisine curated; base times = slow-cooker method, per-method overrides in methods[].

recipes.name: Hawaiian Kalua Pork
recipes.description: A smoky, tender, minimal-ingredient pork roast that tastes like it came straight from an island luau. Perfect for pairing with white rice and a side of teriyaki sauce.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Pierce the pork all over with a carving fork.
Rub the salt and liquid smoke over the meat and place it in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 16 hours.
Remove from the slow cooker and shred, mixing the meat with the rendered juices.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Cut the pork into 3-inch chunks and rub with the salt and liquid smoke.
Add 1/2 cup water or broth to the pressure cooker.
Cook on High Pressure for 90 minutes, then allow a natural pressure release for 20 minutes.
Shred the pork.

recipes.funFact: Traditional Kalua pork is cooked in an 'imu', an underground oven, using heated rocks and banana leaves!

recipes.name: Teriyaki Beef
recipes.description: Tender strips of beef simmered in a sweet and savory garlic-ginger soy sauce, ideal for an effortless weeknight dinner.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Combine all ingredients except the beef in the slow cooker and whisk.
Add the sliced beef.
Cook on Low for 4-5 hours.
Thicken the sauce with a cornstarch slurry at the end if desired.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add all ingredients to the pressure cooker.
Cook on High Pressure for 15 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Stir in a cornstarch slurry using the sauté function until thickened.

recipes.funFact: The word 'teriyaki' derives from the noun 'teri' (meaning shine or luster given by the sugar) and 'yaki' (meaning the cooking method of grilling or broiling).

recipes.name: Steak Fajita Mix
recipes.description: Sizzling flavors without the skillet. This method yields incredibly tender beef strips imbued with classic Mexican spices.
ingredients: 2 lbs skirt or flank steak, sliced

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place half the peppers and onions in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Top with the sliced beef, then the spices, broth, and remaining vegetables.
Cook on Low for 6 hours.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add the broth, beef, spices, and vegetables to the pot.
Cook on High Pressure for 10 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Sauté for 3 minutes to reduce the liquid.

recipes.funFact: Fajita originally referred specifically to the cut of beef used (skirt steak), coming from the Spanish word 'faja' for girdle or strip.

recipes.name: Italian Sausage and Peppers
recipes.description: A classic Italian-American comfort dish. The slow cooking mellows the peppers and onions, turning them into a sweet compote that beautifully coats savory sausage.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Sear the sausages in a skillet first (optional but recommended).
Place all ingredients in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6 hours or High for 3 hours.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Use the sauté function to brown the sausages.
Add the peppers, onions, tomatoes, and oregano.
Cook on High Pressure for 15 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.

recipes.funFact: Sausage and peppers is a staple at the Feast of San Gennaro, a massive annual Italian-American festival in New York City's Little Italy.

recipes.name: Roast Beef French Dip
recipes.description: Melt-in-your-mouth roast beef cooked in a rich, onion-infused broth. The broth doubles as the perfect savory au jus for dipping.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place the roast in the slow cooker.
In a bowl, mix the consommé, broth, soy sauce, and soup mix, then pour over the roast.
Cook on Low for 8-10 hours.
Shred and serve on hoagies with the broth for dipping.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Cut the roast into 4 large pieces.
Add all ingredients to the pot.
Cook on High Pressure for 60 minutes.
Natural release for 15 minutes, then shred the meat.

recipes.funFact: The French Dip was invented in Los Angeles in the early 20th century. Two rival restaurants, Philippe the Original and Cole's, both claim to have invented it!

recipes.name: Split Pea Soup with Ham
recipes.description: A hearty, thick, and nourishing soup where the dried peas break down entirely to form a creamy base flavored with smoky ham.
ingredients: 1 meaty ham bone or 1.5 lbs diced ham

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Layer the vegetables and peas in the slow cooker.
Nestle the ham bone in the center and pour in the broth and water.
Cook on Low for 7-8 hours until the peas are fully broken down.
Remove the bone, dice the meat, and return it to the soup.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add all ingredients to the pot.
Cook on High Pressure for 15 minutes.
Natural release for 15 minutes. (Peas cook extremely fast under pressure!)

recipes.funFact: Pea soup has been consumed since antiquity; the ancient Greeks and Romans cultivated peas heavily for drying and storing.

recipes.name: Turkey Breast
recipes.description: A foolproof method for keeping turkey breast moist and tender, perfect for slicing thick for homestyle meals or thin for exceptional sandwiches.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Rub the turkey breast with the oil and seasonings.
Pour the broth into the bottom of the slow cooker and place the turkey in.
Cook on Low for 6-7 hours until the internal temperature reaches 165°F.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Pour the broth into the pot and place a trivet inside.
Set the seasoned turkey breast on the trivet.
Cook on High Pressure for 35 minutes.
Natural release for 10 minutes.

recipes.funFact: Turkey is known for containing tryptophan, an amino acid, but it actually contains about the same amount of tryptophan as chicken or beef!

recipes.name: Classic Pot Roast with Roots
recipes.description: The ultimate Sunday dinner. Beef chuck becomes incredibly tender as it braises alongside carrots, potatoes, and savory herbs.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Sear the roast in a hot skillet first.
Place the vegetables in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Top with the roast, broth, and rosemary.
Cook on Low for 8-9 hours.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Sauté the roast in the pot until browned.
Remove the roast and add the broth to deglaze.
Return the meat and add the vegetables on top.
Cook on High Pressure for 60 minutes.
Natural release for 15 minutes.

recipes.funFact: Pot roast isn't a specific cut of meat; it's a cooking method (braising) applied to tougher cuts like chuck, brisket, or round.

recipes.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.description: A deeply spiced, creamy tomato curry. Slow cooking allows the spices to bloom and penetrate the chicken completely.
ingredients: 1/2 cup heavy cream (stirred in at the end)

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Combine all ingredients except the cream in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6 hours.
Stir in the heavy cream 15 minutes before serving.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add the chicken, tomatoes, onion, garlic, and spices.
Cook on High Pressure for 10 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Stir in the heavy cream on the 'Keep Warm' setting.

recipes.funFact: Chicken Tikka Masala is often considered the national dish of Britain, having been widely popularized by South Asian chefs in the UK.

recipes.name: Classic Beef Stew
recipes.description: A thick, hearty, and robust stew loaded with tender chunks of beef and root vegetables in a deeply flavored gravy.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Toss the meat with 2 tbsp of flour and sear in a pan.
Transfer to the slow cooker with the broth, tomato paste, carrots, and potatoes.
Cook on Low for 8 hours.
Stir in the peas 10 minutes before serving.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Sauté the meat in the pot.
Add the broth, tomato paste, carrots, and potatoes.
Cook on High Pressure for 35 minutes.
Natural release for 10 minutes, then stir in the peas.

recipes.funFact: The oldest known evidence of stew was found in Japan, dating back to the Jōmon period (c. 14,000–300 BCE).

recipes.name: Chili Con Carne
recipes.description: A robust, highly seasoned chili packed with ground beef, beans, and bacon for an extra layer of smoky depth.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs ground beef, browned and drained

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Combine the browned beef, chopped bacon, beans, tomatoes, and spices in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6-8 hours to let the flavors meld.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Sauté the beef and bacon in the pot, then drain the excess fat.
Add the beans, tomatoes, and spices.
Cook on High Pressure for 15 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.

recipes.funFact: The first recorded instance of 'chili con carne' being eaten by Americans was at the 1893 Columbian Exposition in Chicago at the 'San Antonio Chili Stand'.

recipes.name: Pork Carnitas
recipes.description: Mexican pulled pork infused with citrus and oregano. The trick is crispening the shredded pork under a broiler right before serving.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place the pork in the slow cooker.
Pour the citrus juices, garlic, and spices over the top.
Cook on Low for 8-10 hours.
Shred, then spread on a baking sheet and broil for 5 minutes until the edges are crispy.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Cut the pork into cubes.
Add the juices and spices.
Cook on High Pressure for 45 minutes.
Natural release for 15 minutes, then shred and broil.

recipes.funFact: 'Carnitas' literally translates to 'little meats' in Spanish.

recipes.name: Chicken Tortilla Soup
recipes.description: A zesty, comforting soup brimming with shredded chicken, black beans, corn, and a bold tomato-jalapeño broth.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place all ingredients in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6 hours.
Remove the chicken, shred it, and return it to the soup.
Serve with crushed tortilla chips.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Place all ingredients in the pot.
Cook on High Pressure for 12 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Shred the chicken and return it to the soup.

recipes.funFact: Tortilla soup (Sopa de Tortilla) originated in the state of Tlaxcala in Mexico, a name which means 'place of the maize tortilla'.

recipes.name: Vegetarian Black Bean & Quinoa Chili
recipes.description: A protein-packed, plant-based chili. The quinoa expands to create an incredibly hearty and satisfying texture.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Combine all ingredients in the slow cooker.
Cook on High for 3-4 hours or Low for 6-7 hours.
The quinoa will absorb the liquid and thicken the chili.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Combine all ingredients in the pot.
Cook on High Pressure for 8 minutes.
Natural release for 10 minutes.

recipes.funFact: Quinoa is a pseudocereal, meaning it's biologically a seed rather than a true grain, but it is cooked and eaten like a grain.

recipes.name: BBQ Baby Back Ribs
recipes.description: Fall-off-the-bone tender ribs without needing a smoker. A final flash under the broiler caramelizes the BBQ sauce perfectly.
ingredients: 1 cup of your favorite BBQ sauce

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs and rub with the spices.
Coil the ribs to fit into the slow cooker and pour 1/2 cup BBQ sauce over them.
Cook on Low for 8 hours.
Carefully remove, baste with the remaining sauce, and broil for 5 minutes.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Remove the membrane and rub the ribs with the spices.
Place 1 cup water and a trivet in the pot, then coil the ribs on the trivet.
Cook on High Pressure for 25 minutes.
Natural release for 10 minutes, then broil with the sauce.

recipes.funFact: Baby back ribs are named not because they come from a baby pig, but because they are shorter than spareribs.

recipes.name: Creamy Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.description: A rich, custard-style mac and cheese that cooks perfectly in the slow cooker without the need to boil the pasta beforehand.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Spray the insert with cooking spray.
Mix all ingredients in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 2 hours, stirring once halfway through.
Do not overcook or the pasta will become mushy.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add the pasta, 4 cups water, and a pinch of salt.
Cook on High Pressure for 4 minutes.
Quick release the pressure; do not drain.
Stir in the evaporated milk and cheeses until melted.

recipes.funFact: Thomas Jefferson is credited with helping to popularize Macaroni and Cheese in the US after encountering pasta machines in Paris.

recipes.name: Indian Butter Chicken
recipes.description: Murgh Makhani: a velvety, heavily spiced (but not spicy-hot) tomato and cream sauce enveloping tender chunks of chicken.
ingredients: 1/2 cup heavy cream (stirred in at the end)

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Add the chicken, tomato sauce, garlic, ginger, and spices to the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6 hours.
Stir in the heavy cream just before serving.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add the chicken, sauce, and spices to the pot.
Cook on High Pressure for 10 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Stir in the heavy cream.

recipes.funFact: Butter Chicken was invented by chance in Delhi in the 1950s by mixing leftover tandoori chicken with a tomato gravy.

recipes.name: Corned Beef and Cabbage
recipes.description: A St. Patrick's Day staple that benefits immensely from low, slow cooking to tenderize the heavily cured brisket.
ingredients: 1 (3-4 lb) corned beef brisket (with spice packet)
1 small head green cabbage, cut into wedges

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place the potatoes and carrots in the slow cooker.
Top with the brisket and spice packet, then pour in the broth.
Cook on Low for 8-9 hours.
Add the cabbage wedges during the last hour of cooking.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Place the brisket, potatoes, carrots, and broth in the pot.
Cook on High Pressure for 90 minutes.
Quick release, then add the cabbage.
Cook on High Pressure for 3 more minutes.

recipes.funFact: Corned beef got its name from the large 'corns' (grains) of rock salt traditionally used to cure the meat.

recipes.name: Swedish Meatballs
recipes.description: Tender meatballs simmered in a rich, savory cream sauce with hints of allspice and nutmeg.

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place the meatballs in the slow cooker.
Whisk the broth, Worcestershire, and spices together and pour over.
Cook on Low for 4 hours.
Stir in the heavy cream and a cornstarch slurry during the last 30 minutes to thicken.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add the meatballs, broth, and spices.
Cook on High Pressure for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Sauté, stirring in the heavy cream and a cornstarch slurry until thick.

recipes.funFact: In Sweden, meatballs are traditionally served with lingonberry jam, which adds a tart contrast to the rich gravy.

recipes.name: White Chicken Chili
recipes.description: A creamy, comforting alternative to traditional red chili, featuring green chiles, white beans, and chicken.
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans great northern beans, drained
1/2 cup sour cream (stir in at end)

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place the chicken, beans, chiles, broth, and cumin in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6-8 hours.
Shred the chicken.
Stir in the sour cream before serving.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add all ingredients except the sour cream.
Cook on High Pressure for 15 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Shred the chicken and stir in the sour cream.

recipes.funFact: White chili originated in the American Southwest and often utilizes Hatch green chiles from New Mexico.

recipes.name: Chipotle Barbacoa Beef
recipes.description: Incredibly tender, spicy, and tangy shredded beef. Perfect for tacos, burritos, or rice bowls.
ingredients: 3 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, chopped

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Cut the roast into large chunks.
Mix the vinegar, chipotles, garlic, and spices, and pour over the beef.
Cook on Low for 8-9 hours until it falls apart easily.
Shred the meat.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Cut the beef into smaller chunks.
Add the sauce mixture and 1/2 cup broth.
Cook on High Pressure for 60 minutes.
Natural release for 15 minutes, then shred.

recipes.funFact: The word 'barbecue' actually derives from 'barbacoa', the term used by the Taíno people of the Caribbean to describe a wooden framework for roasting meat.

recipes.name: Classic Beef Stroganoff
recipes.description: Tender beef chunks smothered in a deeply savory mushroom and sour cream gravy, traditionally served over egg noodles.
ingredients: 1 cup sour cream (stir in at end)

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Combine the beef, mushrooms, onion, broth, and mustard in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 7-8 hours.
Turn off the heat and stir in the sour cream (to prevent curdling).

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Sauté the beef to brown.
Add the mushrooms, onion, broth, and mustard.
Cook on High Pressure for 20 minutes.
Natural release for 10 minutes, then stir in the sour cream.

recipes.funFact: The dish is named after the Stroganov family, one of the richest families in Tsarist Russia.

recipes.name: Spiced Apple Butter
recipes.description: A deeply caramelized, spreadable reduction of apples, cinnamon, and cloves. Your house will smell incredible.
ingredients: 5 lbs apples (mixed varieties like Granny Smith and Honeycrisp), peeled and cored

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place the chopped apples in the slow cooker and top with the sugar and spices.
Cook on Low for 10 hours.
Puree with an immersion blender.
Cook on Low for 2 more hours uncovered to thicken.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Place the apples, sugar, and spices in the pot with 1/2 cup water.
Cook on High Pressure for 15 minutes.
Quick release, then puree.
Sauté uncovered until thick.

recipes.funFact: Despite its name, apple butter contains absolutely no dairy butter; the name refers to its smooth, spreadable texture.

recipes.name: Classic Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.description: The ultimate cold-weather cure. Cooking the chicken directly in the broth results in an intensely flavorful soup.
ingredients: 2 cups egg noodles (added at the end)

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place the chicken, vegetables, and broth in the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6-8 hours.
Remove and shred the chicken.
Stir in the egg noodles and cook on High for 15 minutes until the noodles are tender.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Add the chicken, vegetables, and broth.
Cook on High Pressure for 10 minutes.
Quick release, then remove the chicken to shred.
Add the noodles and sauté for 5 minutes until tender, then return the chicken.

recipes.funFact: Chicken soup has been prescribed as a medical remedy for the common cold since the 12th century by the physician Maimonides.

recipes.name: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice
recipes.description: A true New Orleans classic. The slow cooking breaks down the kidney beans to create a rich, creamy gravy that coats the smoked sausage.
ingredients: 1 lb dried red kidney beans, rinsed

methods.label: Slow Cooker
steps: Place all ingredients into the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 8-10 hours until the beans are tender.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Serve over cooked white rice.

methods.label: Pressure Cooker
steps: Place all ingredients into the pressure cooker.
Cook on High Pressure for 45 minutes.
Natural release for 15 minutes.
Mash some beans to thicken, and serve over cooked white rice.

recipes.funFact: Historically in New Orleans, red beans and rice was traditionally served on Mondays using the leftover ham bone from Sunday dinner.
